title: Routing & Validation in Express vs NestJS

scenes.line1: How do you stop bad data early?
scenes.say: When handling requests, how do you make sure only valid data gets through? And why does the way you set up routes matter?
Express routes are just functions, and validation runs as middleware. In NestJS, routes live inside controllers, and validation happens through pipes.
Here, Express uses a validator middleware to check the email field. If validation fails, the request is rejected before any business logic runs.
In NestJS, you define a data transfer object with decorators, add a validation pipe to your route, and your controller only sees valid data.

scenes.question: Should you validate after business logic?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it's fine to validate late.
scenes.right: No, always validate before business logic to avoid bugs and wasted processing.
scenes.say: Don't wait to validate until after your main code runs. Always check incoming data first, so you don't process anything invalid.
